_readme: Copy this to seed.json (gitignored) and fill in real data. This repo is PUBLIC.
chore_definitions is the slice-2 model: ONE definition per real-world chore,
with assignment rows carrying who-does-it-on-which-day. 'Kitchen reset' below
is ONE definition split across two adults — NOT two definitions. Splitting it
means maintaining the same chore twice, and the day the two copies diverge is
the day the arguing restarts.
days: 'mon'..'sun', or the shorthand 'all'. Deliberately NOT the 0-6 integers
the database stores — a hand-edited file should not be the place where someone
has to remember whether 0 means Monday or Sunday.
week: 'every' (or omit it), 'even', or 'odd' — alternating weeks. Which real
week is 'even' is an accident of the calendar, so after seeding run
materialize.py --date <next Saturday> --dry-run; if the zones come back
swapped from reality, swap even/odd here and re-seed. Do that BEFORE the
first real Saturday, not after.
cadence is descriptive only ('daily' | 'weekly'). The schedule is the days.
cutoff_time is LIVE. "HH:MM" 24-hour wall clock, or null for no deadline.
The materializer resolves it per instance into cutoff_at, in the household
timezone, so a rule like 18:15 stays 6:15 PM across both DST changes. null
means no deadline and never 'already late'.
Set it to when the chore must be DONE, not when it starts. A cutoff at the
start time turns the chore red the moment someone picks up a broom, and a
board that is red every day is one nobody reads.
sort_order IS live — it is the order chores appear in on the kiosk. Leave
gaps (10, 20, 30) so a new chore can slot between two without renumbering.
Put end-of-day chores last: alphabetically the nightly family reset lands in
the middle of the afternoon, which is not when it happens.
A dependent must never appear in assignments: the API refuses a dependent
completion and the kiosk gives them nothing to press, so the chore would
materialize into a row nobody can ever clear. seed.py refuses it.
